value: A stack of Transformer decoder blocks in which every parameter is used for every token, trained to predict the next token from the left context. The Transformer itself replaced recurrence with attention (Vaswani et al., 2017); GPT-4's technical report describes 'a Transformer-based model pre-trained to predict the next token', and Meta describes Llama 3.1 405B as 'a dense Transformer with 405B parameters'. For a dense model, total parameters equal parameters used per token, so size and per-token compute move together.
Llama 3.1 405B, Qwen3-32B, Gemma 3 27B, OLMo 2 32B, Phi-4, Apertus 70B

Feed-forward layers are split into many 'experts' and a learned router sends each token to a few of them, so only a fraction of the weights run per token (Shazeer et al., 2017; Switch Transformer, 2021). Two numbers therefore matter: total parameters (memory needed to hold the model) and active parameters (compute per token). Mixtral 8x7B has 47B total but 'only uses 13B active parameters'; DeepSeek-V3 has 671B total and 37B activated; Kimi K3.1 Pro has 2.8T total and 104B activated. Comparing a MoE's total count with a dense model's count overstates its per-token cost.
Mixtral 8x7B, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-235B-A22B, gpt-oss-120b, Llama 4 Maverick, Mistral Large 4

Models that replace most quadratic self-attention layers with layers whose cost grows linearly with sequence length — selective state-space (Mamba) layers or linear-attention variants such as Gated DeltaNet, lightning attention or Kimi Delta Attention — keeping a few full-attention layers for exact recall. Mamba introduced selective state spaces (Gu & Dao, 2023); Jamba interleaved Transformer and Mamba blocks with MoE; Nemotron-H 'replace[s] the majority of self-attention layers… with Mamba layers'; Falcon-H1 runs attention and SSM heads in parallel; Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.8 use three Gated DeltaNet layers per gated-attention layer. The payoff is cheaper long-context inference. Sliding-window or compressed-attention schemes (Gemma, DeepSeek-V4) are still attention and are not counted here.
Jamba 1.5 Large, Nemotron-H 56B, Falcon-H1-34B, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, MiniMax-M1, Granite 4.0-H-Small, Kimi K3.1 Pro

Instead of emitting one token at a time left to right, the model starts from masked or noised text and refines many positions in parallel over several denoising steps. LLaDA (Nie et al., 2025) trained an 8B masked-diffusion model 'from scratch under the pre-training and SFT paradigm'; Inception's Mercury Coder is a commercial diffusion LLM reporting 1,109 tokens/s; Google showed Gemini Diffusion at I/O (May 2025) and released DiffusionGemma 26B A4B with open weights (June 2026), which denoises 256 tokens at a time. The main selling point is generation speed.
LLaDA 8B, Mercury Coder, Gemini Diffusion, DiffusionGemma 26B A4B

Pre-LLM-era Transformer designs that are not generative chat models in the modern sense. BERT is encoder-only: it reads the whole input bidirectionally ('jointly conditioning on both left and right context') and is fine-tuned for classification, retrieval or extraction. T5 is encoder–decoder: it 'converts all text-based language problems into a text-to-text format'. They survive in embeddings, rerankers and some translation systems; none of the generative models in the table uses them.

Closed developers usually do not publish architecture or size. Google disclosed that Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 are sparse MoE Transformers but not their sizes; OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI publish neither. Report AI does not estimate parameter counts for closed models; third-party figures (e.g. Epoch's database values) are cited only as labelled estimates.
GPT-5, Claude Opus 5.5, Grok 4, Gemini 4 Argon

value: The raw output of pre-training: a next-token predictor over a large corpus with no instruction following or safety tuning. Useful for research and as a starting point for fine-tunes. Open developers often publish base checkpoints next to tuned ones (Llama, Qwen, Gemma '-pt', OLMo, Nemotron-H base-only); closed developers essentially never do.

A base model further trained with supervised examples and preference optimisation (RLHF or variants) to follow instructions and converse. OpenAI's InstructGPT paper showed outputs from a 1.3B instruction-tuned model were preferred to those of the 175B base GPT-3. Answers come straight away, with no separate reasoning phase. In the table this is reasoning = 'none'.
GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 4 Maverick, Kimi K2

Trained, usually with large-scale reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks, to produce a long chain of reasoning before the final answer, trading inference compute ('test-time compute') for accuracy. DeepSeek-R1 showed reasoning 'can be incentivized through pure reinforcement learning'; Snell et al. (2024) found scaling test-time compute can beat scaling parameters. In the table, 'reasoning' means the model always reasons (effort may be adjustable but cannot be turned off).
o1, o3, DeepSeek-R1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Opus 5.5, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B

One set of weights that can either answer immediately or think first, controlled by a switch or a thinking-token budget. Anthropic called Claude 3.7 Sonnet 'the first hybrid reasoning model on the market' (Feb 2025); Qwen3 integrated 'thinking mode… and non-thinking mode… into a unified framework' with a thinking budget; Gemini 2.5 Flash is Google's 'hybrid reasoning model with a controllable thinking budget'.
Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Qwen3-235B-A22B, DeepSeek-V3.1, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemma 4, Claude Haiku 5.5

A training emphasis rather than a separate mode: post-training on multi-step tasks in which the model calls tools, browses, runs code or operates a terminal, often with RL in real or simulated environments. Kimi K2 used 'a large-scale agentic data synthesis pipeline and a joint reinforcement learning stage'; gpt-oss was optimised for 'deep research browsing, python tool use'; Jais 3 is trained to 'call tools and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, operate a terminal'. Recorded in the table as agentic_trained = true only where the developer says so.
Kimi K2, GLM-4.5, MiniMax-M2, gpt-oss-120b, Jais-3-375B-A23B, Nemotron 3 Nano

value: Weights are not released; access is through the developer's app or API, sometimes further restricted (Claude Mythos 5 to vetted partners; Muse Spark to a private API preview; Apple's on-device model only inside Apple's framework). The developer can change, rate-limit or retire the model (Claude 3 Opus was retired on 5 Jan 2026).
GPT-5, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3 Pro, Grok 4, Muse Spark

Trained parameters can be downloaded and run locally, but training data and full training code are not released, and the licence may restrict use. Permissive examples use OSI-approved licences (Apache 2.0: gpt-oss, Qwen3, Gemma 4; MIT: DeepSeek-R1, GLM). Restricted examples use custom terms: the Llama licences require a separate Meta licence above 700 million monthly active users; Gemma (before Gemma 4) used Gemma Terms of Use; Muse Spark Open, Mistral Large 4 and Kimi K3.1 Pro add model-as-a-service or attribution conditions; some are non-commercial (Mistral Research Licence, CC-BY-NC for Command A).
Llama 4 Maverick, DeepSeek-R1, gpt-oss-120b, Mistral Large 4, Kimi K3.1 Pro

The Open Source Initiative's Open Source AI Definition 1.0 (released October 2024) requires the 'preferred form for making modifications': data information sufficient for 'a skilled person [to] build a substantially equivalent system', the complete training and inference code, and the parameters, under OSI-approved terms. In OSI's validation, Pythia, OLMo, Amber, CrystalCoder and T5 passed, while Llama 2, Grok, Phi-2 and Mixtral did not. The Linux Foundation's Model Openness Framework (used for IBM Granite's 'Class 3' badge) is a graded alternative. (OSI pages were read via search summaries only.)

value: Text (and code) in, text out. Most open-weight LLMs through 2025 and many specialised models.

Accepts images (and in some cases audio or video) alongside text but answers only in text. GPT-4 accepted 'image and text inputs and produce[d] text outputs'; Gemini 1.5 handled 'hours of video and audio'; most 2026 frontier models are in this class.
GPT-4, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Llama 4 Scout, Muse Spark Open

One network that takes and produces speech (and other media) natively instead of chaining separate speech-to-text and text-to-speech models. OpenAI said GPT-4o 'accepts as input any combination of text, audio, image, and video and generates any combination of text, audio, and image outputs', answering audio in as little as 232 ms.

Generates images as well as text from the same model family (as opposed to a separate diffusion image model). Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash Image and Gemini 3 Pro Image ('Nano Banana', 'Nano Banana Pro') list image and text output.
Gemini 3 Pro Image (Nano Banana Pro), GPT-4o (image output, 2025)

Epoch AI defines frontier models as those 'in the top 5 by training compute at the time of their release'. Because Epoch has no compute estimate for most 2025–26 closed flagships, Report AI's table also counts a model as frontier if Epoch estimates it at ≥10²⁵ FLOP, or if it is the top-tier closed flagship of a developer with a ≥10²⁵ run on record (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, Meta). This rule is Report AI's (DERIVED).
GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, Llama 3.1 405B, Kimi K3.1 Pro
Open-weight models at or above 100B total parameters that do not meet the frontier rule. Most are MoE, so active parameters can be far smaller (gpt-oss-120b runs 5.1B per token).
Models that fit on one or a few data-centre GPUs; the bulk of self-hosted enterprise deployments.

There is no regulatory definition. NVIDIA researchers define an SLM functionally as one that 'can fit onto a common consumer electronic device and perform inference with latency sufficiently low to be practical', adding they would be 'comfortable with considering most models below 10bn parameters' SLMs as of 2025. Report AI uses <10B total parameters.

Designed and shipped to run locally on phones or laptops, typically 2–4B effective parameters with aggressive quantisation. Gemini Nano comes in '1.8B (Nano-1) and 3.25B (Nano-2)' versions, 4-bit quantised; Apple's 2025 on-device model is '~3B' with 2-bit quantisation-aware training; Phi-3-mini was billed as running 'locally on your phone'; Gemma 3n E4B runs 8B raw parameters at a 4B footprint.
Gemini Nano, Apple Foundation Model (on-device), Phi-3-mini, Gemma 3n E4B
Closed models sold as the fast/cheap tier whose size is not published (Haiku, Flash, Mercury). Classified by tier, not by parameters.
Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Mercury Coder
Broad chat, writing, reasoning and coding ability; nearly all frontier models.
Trained or tuned mainly for programming and agentic coding.

Systems specialised for formal or competition mathematics. None is in the table; Report AI's models data cites DeepMind's AlphaProof (IMO 2024 silver standard, 28/42) as an example — a formal-proof system rather than a general LLM.
Tuned and evaluated for one professional domain. Med-PaLM 2 targeted medical question answering at USMLE level.
Output vectors (or relevance scores) instead of text, for search and retrieval-augmented generation. Qwen3 Embedding builds embedding and reranking models 'upon the Qwen3 foundation models'.
Classifiers that label prompts and responses against a hazard taxonomy, deployed beside a chat model. Llama Guard 4 is 'a natively multimodal safety classifier with 12 billion parameters'.

value: Under Article 51 of the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), a general-purpose AI model is presumed to have high-impact capabilities, and so 'systemic risk', when its cumulative training compute exceeds 10²⁵ floating-point operations; such providers must evaluate and red-team models, report serious incidents and ensure cybersecurity. Secondary sources report the 2026 Digital Omnibus deal (provisional agreement 7 May 2026) changed deadlines, not this threshold. (EUR-Lex was not reachable; MEDIUM.)

value: Executive Order 14110 (30 Oct 2023) set interim reporting duties for models trained with more than 10²⁶ integer or floating-point operations (10²³ for models trained primarily on biological sequence data). It was rescinded on 20 January 2025; sources differ on whether EO 14148 or EO 14179 was the instrument. No federal compute threshold is in force as far as found.

California's Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act, signed 29 Sep 2025 and in force since 1 Jan 2026, defines a 'frontier model' as one trained with more than 10²⁶ integer or floating-point operations, counting fine-tuning and later modifications; 'large frontier developers' (over $500M annual revenue) carry extra duties. New York's RAISE Act (final amendment signed 27 Mar 2026, effective 1 Jan 2027) uses 10²⁶ plus a >$100M compute-cost test.

Most open-weight models, including very large MoEs, sit below 10²⁵ because active parameters, not total, drive training FLOP: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T total) is estimated at 9.7 × 10²⁴. Most 2025–26 closed flagships have no public estimate at all.
